extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: MathVista is a benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering diverse mathematical reasoning types, tasks, and visual contexts.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu (UCLA; Microsoft Research, Redmond); Hritik Bansal (UCLA); Tony Xia (UCLA); Jiacheng Liu (University of Washington); Chunyuan Li (Microsoft Research, Redmond); Hannaneh Hajishirzi (University of Washington); Hao Cheng (Microsoft Research, Redmond); Kai-Wei Chang (UCLA); Michel Galley (Microsoft Research, Redmond); Jianfeng Gao (Microsoft Research, Redmond)
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, and Jianfeng Gao. 2024. MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA was assembled by collecting nine existing multimodal MathQA datasets, reviewing more than 70 VQA datasets and selecting 19 publicly available math-related ones, and creating three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). For VQA sources, the authors first used heuristic rules to automatically select likely math-related examples, then had three expert annotators manually label them, and capped each source dataset at 400 examples for balanced representation. The new datasets were sourced from online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic illustrations from online education resources.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator; Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw/source data consisted of 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) plus three newly created datasets: IQTest sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms, FunctionQA consisting of functional plots, and PaperQA derived from academic illustrations including tables, figures, and charts from online education resources, with 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules automatically selected examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning, then three expert annotators manually labeled whether the examples involve mathematical reasoning, with majority voting used to finalize the collection; for the three new datasets, all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, with disagreements resolved through discussion among the entire review team; for metadata, expert annotators manually labeled mathematical reasoning categories for 1,000 examples using an annotation tool; for the human performance baseline and Bard assessment, Amazon Mechanical Turk annotators with satisfactory annotating history, qualification examples passed, and a high school diploma or higher completed tasks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk; annotation tool; GPT-4V playground chatbot; Multimodal Bard chatbot
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For VQA dataset labeling, majority voting was used to finalize the collection. For the three new datasets, a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2% was reported, with 6 disagreements among 736 questions resolved through discussion to reach consensus. For labeling whether problems involve mathematical reasoning, inter-annotator agreement was analyzed with Fleiss Kappa, yielding 0.775. For mathematical reasoning metadata, 94.1% of examples from automatic and human annotations had the exact same set of reasoning types, and 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: graduate students in STEM fields; high school diploma or higher; AMT annotators with more than 5,000 HIT tasks completed and acceptance score higher than 0.99
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: heuristic rules; GPT-4 answer extractor; EasyOCR; Multimodal Bard
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals; the scalability and generalizability of our benchmark to other domains remain a concern; only 85.6% of examples have annotations; annotations lack a unified format and structure; the study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: AI agents with strong mathematical reasoning capabilities in visual contexts have a wide range of real-world applications, such as solving complex problems in educational disciplines, helping analysts with logical queries about statistical data, and assisting in theorem proving and scientific discovery in advanced research fields
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: a benchmark for model development validation; standard evaluation of foundation models' mathematical reasoning capabilities in visual contexts; facilitate the development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios; evaluate the research progress of LLMs and LMMs, especially their capabilities in solving rigorous reasoning tasks
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: the answer labels for test will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and we will maintain an online evaluation platform; we are committed to maintaining the datasets, such as refining the potential data noise, in response to the community feedback; we are committed to evolving the leaderboard in response to new models
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure a balanced representation of each source in our final compiled benchmark. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning, then three expert annotators manually labeled them, and using majority voting and limiting each source dataset to 400 examples, the authors finalized a collection of 2,739 examples. For release, testmini was created by randomly sampling 4 questions from each source dataset and then randomly sampling the remaining questions for each source dataset based on its proportion in the entire set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, the authors initially designed heuristic rules to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates: examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words in the questions were selected. They also state that they conducted several quality checks to address any unidentified errors.
